questions.question: Which device relies on the heating effect of current to protect circuits and appliances by intentionally melting to break the circuit when the current exceeds a specified limit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electric fuse**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **electric fuse** is a crucial safety device used in electrical circuits to protect against **overcurrent** and **short circuits**.
 
• It operates on the principle of the **heating effect of electric current** (also known as **Joule heating**), where the heat produced is proportional to the square of the current (**H = I²Rt**).
 
• The fuse consists of a thin wire made of a material with a **low melting point** and **high resistance**, typically an **alloy of lead and tin** (usually **37% lead and 63% tin**).
 
• When the current flowing through the circuit exceeds a **predetermined safe limit**, the temperature of the fuse wire rises rapidly, causing it to **melt** and break the electrical path.
 
• By intentionally melting and "blowing," the fuse effectively **isolates the appliance** from the power source, preventing potential **fire hazards** and damage to sensitive components.
 
• A fuse is always connected in **series** with the **live wire** so that all current entering the circuit must pass through it first.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electric Bulb Filament**:
 
 
• The filament is typically made of **Tungsten** because of its exceptionally **high melting point** (approximately **3422°C**).
 
• Unlike a fuse, it is designed **not to melt**; instead, it becomes **incandescent** (glows white-hot) to produce **light** when current passes through it.
 
 
 
• **Electric Iron Coil**:
 
 
• Heating appliances like irons and heaters use a heating element made of **Nichrome** (an alloy of **nickel, chromium, and iron**).
 
• Nichrome is chosen because it has **high resistivity** and does not **oxidize (burn)** easily even at high temperatures, allowing it to produce steady heat for pressing clothes.
 
 
 
• **Rheostat**:
 
 
• A **Rheostat** is a **variable resistor** used to manually adjust the magnitude of **current** in a circuit without interrupting the power supply.
 
• It does not protect the circuit by melting; rather, it functions by **altering the resistance** within the circuit path.
 
 
 
• **Fuse Ratings**:
 
 
• Fuses are categorized by their **current rating** (measured in **Amperes**). For example, a **5A fuse** is used for low-power circuits (lights, fans), while a **15A fuse** is used for heavy-duty appliances like **air conditioners** and **geysers**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Overloading**: This occurs when too many high-power appliances are connected to a single socket, drawing a total current that exceeds the **capacity of the wires**. The fuse melts to prevent the wires from **overheating**.
 
• **Short Circuiting**: This happens when the **live wire** and **neutral wire** come into direct contact due to damaged insulation. This causes an immediate and massive **surge in current**, which the fuse terminates by melting instantly.
 
• **Modern Alternatives**: In many modern electrical installations, the traditional fuse has been replaced by **Miniature Circuit Breakers (MCBs)**. Unlike fuses, **MCBs** are switches that trip during a fault and can be **reset** manually without the need for replacement.

questions.question: What is the nature of the distance-time graph for an object in non-uniform motion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A curved line**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-uniform motion** is defined as the type of motion where an object covers **unequal distances** in **equal intervals of time**. This implies that the **speed** or **velocity** of the object is **not constant** throughout its journey.
 
• In a **distance-time graph**, the **distance** is plotted on the **Y-axis** and **time** is plotted on the **X-axis**. The **slope** of this graph at any given point represents the **speed** of the object.
 
• For an object in **non-uniform motion**, since the speed changes continuously, the slope of the graph must also change. A graph with a **changing slope** is represented as a **curved line** rather than a straight one.
 
• If the **speed increases** over time (acceleration), the curve of the distance-time graph bends **upwards** (becoming steeper). If the **speed decreases** (deceleration), the curve flattens out as time progresses.
 
• The **non-linear relationship** between distance and time in such cases is often expressed through higher-order equations, such as **quadratic equations** for motion with constant acceleration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uniform Motion**:
 
 
• In **uniform motion**, an object covers **equal distances** in **equal intervals of time**. 
 
• The **distance-time graph** for uniform motion is always a **straight line** passing through the **origin** (if the initial distance is zero). The **constant slope** indicates a **constant speed**.
 
 
 
• **Object at Rest**:
 
 
• When an object is **stationary**, its distance from a reference point does not change as **time** increases.
 
• The graph for an object at rest is a **horizontal line** parallel to the **time axis (X-axis)**. Here, the **slope is zero**, indicating that the **speed is zero**.
 
 
 
• **Vertical Line Paradox**:
 
 
• A **vertical line** on a distance-time graph would mean that an object is covering distance while **time remains constant**.
 
• This would imply an **infinite speed**, which is **physically impossible** according to the laws of classical mechanics.
 
 
 
• **Slope and Speed**:
 
 
• The mathematical formula for the **slope** of the distance-time graph is **Speed = Distance / Time**.
 
• In **calculus**, the **instantaneous speed** is the derivative of distance with respect to time (**v = ds/dt**). For non-uniform motion, this derivative is a function of time, resulting in the **curved nature** of the plot.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Acceleration**: In **non-uniform motion** involving **constant acceleration**, the distance-time graph takes the shape of a **parabola**. This is derived from the second equation of motion: **s = ut + ½at²**, where **s** is distance, **u** is initial velocity, **a** is acceleration, and **t** is time.
 
• **Real-world Examples**: Most real-world movements, such as a **car moving in traffic**, a **train pulling into a station**, or a **ball thrown upwards**, are examples of **non-uniform motion** and will produce **curved lines** on a distance-time graph.

questions.question: Which process must accompany DNA copying to ensure the formation of functional daughter cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Creation of additional cellular apparatus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **DNA copying** (also known as **DNA replication**) is the fundamental process in **reproduction** that creates a genetic blueprint for the next generation. However, a **DNA** molecule by itself cannot maintain life or perform **metabolic functions** without a surrounding environment.
 
• To ensure that **daughter cells** are **functional** and **viable**, the process of **DNA copying** must be accompanied by the **creation of additional cellular apparatus**. This includes the production of **cytoplasm**, **cell membranes**, and various **organelles** like **ribosomes** and **mitochondria**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• **Chromosomal mutation** refers to alterations in the structure or **number** of **chromosomes**. While mutations provide the basis for **evolution**, they are not a required accompaniment to ensure **functional cells**; in many cases, large-scale mutations can lead to **cell death** or **malfunction**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **RNA transcription** and **protein synthesis** are vital **biochemical processes** occurring within a cell. However, "only" performing **transcription** or **translation** is insufficient to form a **new daughter cell**, as a complete physical **cellular structure** is required to house these processes. ***Hence, statements 2 and 3 are incorrect.***
 
• When a **cell divides**, it effectively splits its **cellular apparatus** into **two parts**, each receiving one copy of the **DNA**. Therefore, the **parent cell** must double its **internal components** before **cytokinesis** occurs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid):**
 
 
• It is the **information source** for making **proteins**. If the **information** is changed, different **proteins** will be made, leading to altered **body designs**.
 
• The **process of DNA copying** involves **biochemical reactions** that are never **100% accurate**. This leads to **variations** during **reproduction**, which is the **raw material** for **natural selection** and **evolution**.
 
 
 
• **Cellular Apparatus Components:**
 
 
• The **cellular apparatus** consists of the **cytoplasm**, where most **chemical reactions** occur, and **enzymes** that facilitate **DNA replication**.
 
• In **eukaryotic cells**, this also includes **membrane-bound organelles** like the **Endoplasmic Reticulum**, **Golgi apparatus**, and **Mitochondria** (the **powerhouse of the cell**).
 
 
 
• **Cell Division Cycle:**
 
 
• The **cell cycle** consists of **interphase** (where **DNA** and **organelles** are **doubled**) and the **M-phase** (where **mitosis** or **meiosis** occurs).
 
• **Cytokinesis** is the physical process of **cell division**, which divides the **cytoplasm** of a **parent cell** into **two daughter cells**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Variation:**
 
 
• While **consistency in DNA copying** maintains **species stability**, minor **inaccuracies** allow **populations** to adapt to **environmental changes** over **long periods**.
 
• In **asexual reproduction**, the **daughter cells** are almost **identical**, whereas in **sexual reproduction**, **genetic recombination** increases **diversity**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Biological Significance:** If **DNA** were copied without a **cellular apparatus**, the **DNA copy** would have no **metabolic machinery** to sustain itself, and it would not be considered a **living cell**.
 
• **Historical Context:** The understanding of **DNA** as the **genetic material** was solidified by **scientists** such as **Watson** and **Crick** in **1953**, which helped explain how **hereditary information** is passed during **cell division**.
 
• **Functionality:** A **functional daughter cell** must be able to perform **respiration**, **nutrition**, and **growth** immediately after **division**, all of which require a pre-existing **cellular structure**.
</ul

questions.question: After fertilisation, when other parts of the flower fall off, the ovary grows into what form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fruit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In plants, **fertilization** is the process where the **male gamete** (pollen) fuses with the **female gamete** (egg) inside the **ovule**.
 
• Once fertilization is complete, the flower undergoes several transformations. Most parts, such as the **sepals**, **petals**, and **stamens**, wither and fall away as they are no longer needed.
 
• The **ovary** begins to enlarge and ripen due to hormonal changes, eventually transforming into the **Fruit**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Fruit.***
 
• Simultaneously, the **ovules** located inside the ovary develop into **seeds**. Each seed contains an **embryo**, which is the result of the zygote developing through cell division.
 
• The primary function of the **fruit** is to protect the developing **seeds** and aid in their **dispersal** to ensure the continuation of the plant species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Floral Parts and their Post-Fertilization Fate:**
 
 
• **Ovary Wall:** The wall of the **ovary** develops into the **pericarp** (the fruit wall). In some plants, like **mango**, this becomes fleshy, while in others, like **mustard**, it becomes dry and hard.
 
• **Ovule:** This structure matures into the **seed**. The **integuments** of the ovule harden to form the **seed coat** (testa and tegmen).
 
• **Zygote:** The fertilized egg cell develops into the **embryo**, which consists of the **radicle**, **plumule**, and **cotyledons**.
 
 
 
• **Classification of Fruits:**
 
 
• **True Fruits:** These develop exclusively from the **mature ovary** after fertilization. Examples include **grapes**, **blueberries**, and **tomatoes**.
 
• **False Fruits:** Also known as accessory fruits, these develop from the **ovary** along with other floral parts like the **thalamus** or **receptacle**. Examples include **apple**, **strawberry**, and **cashew**.
 
• **Parthenocarpic Fruits:** These are fruits that develop **without fertilization** and are typically **seedless**, such as **banana**.
 
 
 
• **Explanation of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Anther:** This is the **pollen-producing** part of the **stamen**. It is a male reproductive organ and typically dries up and falls off after the **pollination** stage.
 
• **Style:** This is the **stalk** of the **pistil** that connects the **stigma** to the **ovary**. After fertilization, it usually withers and disappears.
 
• **Pollen Tube:** This is a tubular structure produced by the **pollen grain** to deliver male gametes to the **embryo sac**. It is a temporary structure that degrades once its function is served.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Double Fertilization:** This is a unique feature of **angiosperms** (flowering plants) where one male gamete fuses with the egg to form a **zygote**, and another fuses with two polar nuclei to form the **Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN)**.
 
• **Endosperm:** The **PEN** develops into the **endosperm**, a tissue that provides **nutrition** to the growing **embryo** during seed development.
 
• **Fruit Ripening:** This physiological process involves the breakdown of **chlorophyll**, the softening of the **pericarp**, and the conversion of **starches** into **sugars**, making the fruit attractive to animals for dispersal.
</ul

questions.question: What is the relationship between the radius of curvature and the focal length for spherical mirrors with small apertures?

options.text: Radius of curvature is equal to half the focal length
Radius of curvature is equal to thrice the focal length
Radius of curvature is equal to the focal length
Radius of curvature is equal to twice the focal length

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radius of curvature is equal to twice the focal length**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the study of optics, specifically for **spherical mirrors**, there is a fundamental geometric relationship between the **radius of curvature (R)** and the **focal length (f)**.
 
• The **radius of curvature (R)** is defined as the radius of the hollow sphere of glass of which the reflecting surface of the mirror forms a part. It is the distance from the **pole (P)** to the **center of curvature (C)**.
 
• The **focal length (f)** is the distance between the **pole (P)** and the **principal focus (F)** of the mirror.
 
• For **spherical mirrors** with a **small aperture**, the **principal focus (F)** lies exactly halfway between the **pole (P)** and the **center of curvature (C)**.
 
• This geometric arrangement leads to the mathematical formula: **R = 2f**. This implies that the **radius of curvature** is **twice** the **focal length**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Radius of curvature is equal to twice the focal length.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Spherical Mirrors**:
 
 
• **Concave Mirror**: A spherical mirror with its reflecting surface curved inwards, facing towards the **center of the sphere**. It is also known as a **converging mirror**.
 
• **Convex Mirror**: A spherical mirror with its reflecting surface curved outwards. It is also known as a **diverging mirror**.
 
 
 
• **Aperture**: The diameter of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror is called its **aperture**. The relationship **R = 2f** is an approximation that holds true primarily for mirrors where the **aperture** is much smaller than the **radius of curvature**.
 
• **Principal Axis**: This is the imaginary straight line passing through the **pole** and the **center of curvature** of a spherical mirror.
 
• **Sign Convention**: According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the **focal length** of a **concave mirror** is considered **negative**, while the **focal length** of a **convex mirror** is considered **positive**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Paraxial Rays**: The derivation of the formula **R = 2f** assumes that the light rays are **paraxial**, meaning they strike the mirror very close to the **principal axis** and make small angles with it.
 
• **Spherical Aberration**: If the **aperture** of the mirror is large, the rays falling far from the axis (marginal rays) do not meet at the same **focal point** as the paraxial rays. This defect is known as **spherical aberration**.
 
• **Numerical Application**: If a **convex mirror** has a **radius of curvature** of **32 cm**, its **focal length** would be **16 cm** (f = R/2). Similarly, if a **concave mirror** has a **focal length** of **10 cm**, its **radius of curvature** is **20 cm**.
 
• This relationship is essential for using the **Mirror Formula**: **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**, where **v** is the image distance and **u** is the object distance.
</ul

questions.question: The combining capacity of an element to each other primarily depends on which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Number of valence electrons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **combining capacity** of an atom of an element is known as its **valency**. It describes how many chemical bonds an atom can form with other atoms.
 
• This capacity primarily depends on the **number of valence electrons**, which are the electrons present in the **outermost shell** of an atom. Atoms interact with each other to achieve a stable electronic configuration, typically following the **Octet Rule**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Number of valence electrons.***
 
• According to the **Octet Rule**, atoms are most stable when their outermost shell is completely filled with **eight electrons** (or two for the K-shell). Atoms gain, lose, or share electrons to reach this state.
 
• For elements in **Group 1, 2, and 13**, the valency is usually equal to the number of **valence electrons** (1, 2, and 3 respectively). For elements in **Groups 15, 16, and 17**, the valency is determined by subtracting the number of valence electrons from **8**.
 
• The **chemical reactivity** of an element is fundamentally determined by these electrons. For example, **Sodium (Na)** has **1** valence electron and a valency of **1**, while **Chlorine (Cl)** has **7** valence electrons and a valency of **1** (calculated as 8 - 7).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Number of Protons:**
 
 
• The **number of protons** in the nucleus defines the **atomic number** (Z) of an element and identifies the element itself.
 
• While the positive charge of protons attracts electrons, it is the distribution of those electrons, not the protons themselves, that determines the **combining capacity**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the number of protons is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Number of Energy Levels:**
 
 
• Electrons revolve around the nucleus in specific **energy levels** or **shells** (K, L, M, N). The **number of energy levels** determines the **atomic radius** and the size of the atom.
 
• While the distance of the outermost shell from the nucleus affects how strongly electrons are held, the primary driver for bonding is the specific occupancy of the **valence shell**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the number of energy levels is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Number of Neutrons:**
 
 
• **Neutrons** are subatomic particles found in the nucleus with no electrical charge. The **number of neutrons** contributes to the **atomic mass** (A) of the element.
 
• Varying the number of neutrons results in **isotopes** of the same element, but this does not change the chemical properties or the **valency** of the atom significantly. ***Hence, the statement regarding the number of neutrons is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Noble Gases:**
 
 
• Elements like **Helium (He)**, **Neon (Ne)**, and **Argon (Ar)** have their outermost shells completely filled.
 
• Because they already possess a stable configuration, their **valency is zero**, meaning they have little to no **combining capacity** under normal conditions and are chemically **inert**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Variable Valency:** Some elements, particularly **transition metals** like **Iron (Fe)** or **Copper (Cu)**, exhibit **variable valency** because they can lose electrons from both their outermost shell and the shell just below it.
 
• **Ionic vs. Covalent Bonding:** When atoms **transfer** valence electrons, an **ionic bond** is formed (e.g., NaCl). When they **share** valence electrons, a **covalent bond** is formed (e.g., H₂O).
 
• **Lewis Dot Structures:** This is a common method used to represent the **number of valence electrons** as dots around the symbol of an element, helping to visualize the **combining capacity**.

questions.question: Why does the uterine lining become thick and spongy every month?

options.text: To nourish the embryo if fertilisation occurs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To nourish the embryo if fertilisation occurs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **uterus** is a hollow, pear-shaped organ in the **female reproductive system** where a baby develops during pregnancy. Every month, the inner lining of the **uterus**, known as the **endometrium**, undergoes changes to prepare for a potential pregnancy.
 
• The **uterine lining** becomes **thick, soft, and spongy** due to an increased supply of **blood vessels** and **tissues**. This specialized environment is designed to facilitate the **implantation** of a **fertilized egg** (embryo).
 
• The primary function of this thickened lining is to **nourish the embryo** by providing essential **nutrients** and **oxygen** required for its initial growth and development after **fertilisation**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The **development of the egg** occurs within the **ovaries**, not the uterine lining; therefore, the thickness is not meant to support egg maturation. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• While the lining is rich in nutrients, its purpose is to sustain a **growing fetus** rather than the general **absorption of nutrients** for the mother's metabolic needs. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The thickening of the lining is a precursor to **menstruation** if pregnancy does not occur, rather than a mechanism to **prevent** it. Menstruation is actually the shedding of this very lining. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Menstrual Cycle:**
 
 
• The **menstrual cycle** typically lasts about **28 days**, although it can range from **21 to 35 days** in healthy adults. It is regulated by the interaction of **hormones** from the **pituitary gland** and the **ovaries**.
 
• During the **proliferative phase**, the hormone **estrogen** causes the **endometrium** to grow and thicken.
 
• Following **ovulation** (usually around **day 14**), the **secretory phase** begins, where **progesterone** makes the lining receptive to the **embryo**.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Placenta:**
 
 
• If **implantation** is successful, the **embryo** and the **uterine wall** eventually form the **placenta**. This organ serves as the lifeline between the mother and the **fetus**, exchanging **waste**, **oxygen**, and **nutrients**.
 
 
 
• **Hormonal Regulation:**
 
 
• **Progesterone** is the key hormone responsible for maintaining the **thickened uterine lining**. If **fertilisation** does not occur, the levels of **progesterone** and **estrogen** drop significantly.
 
• This hormonal decline triggers the breakdown of the **endometrium**, leading to **menstruation**, which marks **day 1** of a new cycle.
 
 
 
• **Anatomy and Features:**
 
 
• The **endometrium** is highly **vascularized**, meaning it contains a dense network of **capillaries** to ensure the **embryo** has immediate access to the mother's **blood supply** upon attachment.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is a use of washing soda?

options.text: Used in treatment of hot water
Used to kill bacteria in water

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Removes the hardness of water**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Washing soda**, chemically known as **Sodium carbonate decahydrate** (**Na2CO3.10H2O**), is a crystalline solid that is widely used for domestic and industrial purposes. 
• One of its most significant applications is that it **removes the permanent hardness of water**. Hardness in water is caused by the presence of **calcium** and **magnesium** salts; washing soda reacts with these soluble salts to form insoluble carbonates, which can then be easily removed. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.*** 
• **Washing soda** is not typically **used in cooking**. For culinary purposes, **Sodium bicarbonate** (**NaHCO3**), also known as **baking soda**, is used to make food fluffy and soft. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*** 
• While it is used in water treatment, its specific chemical function is the removal of **calcium and magnesium ions** rather than general "treatment of hot water" in a broad sense. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*** 
• It is not **used to kill bacteria in water**. Chemicals like **Chlorine**, **Potassium permanganate**, or **Bleaching powder** (**Calcium oxychloride**) are used as disinfectants to kill germs and bacteria in drinking water. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*** 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Removes the hardness of water.*** 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Chemical Properties and Synthesis:** 
• **Washing soda** is produced via the **Solvay process**, which involves the reaction of **sodium chloride**, **ammonia**, and **carbon dioxide** in water. 
• The **anhydrous** form of sodium carbonate (**Na2CO3**) is known as **soda ash**. 
• It is a **basic salt**, meaning it turns **red litmus paper to blue** when dissolved in water. 
• **Industrial Applications:** 
• It is a key ingredient in the **glass, soap, and paper industries**. In **glass manufacturing**, it acts as a flux for silica, lowering the melting point of the mixture. 
• It is used in the manufacture of various **sodium compounds**, such as **Borax** (**Na2B4O7.10H2O**). 
• It serves as a powerful **cleaning agent** for domestic laundry because it helps emulsify grease and oils. 
• **Removal of Hardness:** 
• **Permanent hardness** is caused by **chlorides and sulfates** of magnesium and calcium. Since these cannot be removed by boiling, **Sodium carbonate** is added to precipitate the metal ions as **insoluble carbonates**. 
• The reaction can be represented as: **MCl2 + Na2CO3 -> MCO3 (precipitate) + 2NaCl** (where M is Calcium or Magnesium). 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Efflorescence:** When **washing soda crystals** (the decahydrate form) are exposed to air, they lose **nine molecules** of water of crystallization to form a monohydrate (**Na2CO3.H2O**). This process of losing water molecules is called **efflorescence**. 
• **Difference from Baking Soda:** It is crucial to distinguish between **Washing Soda** (**Na2CO3**) and **Baking Soda** (**NaHCO3**). While both are sodium salts, baking soda is safe for **ingestion** and used in **fire extinguishers**, whereas washing soda is primarily for **cleaning and industrial use**. 
• **Water Softening:** In many **detergent** formulations, sodium carbonate is included to prevent the **calcium and magnesium ions** from interfering with the action of the surfactant, ensuring the soap can lather effectively even in **hard water** areas. </ul

questions.question: Which two properties of carbon are mainly responsible for the formation of a large number of carbon compounds?

options.text: Tendency to form ionic bonds and lose electrons
High atomic mass and large atomic size

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tetravalency and catenation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Catenation** is the unique property of **carbon** atoms to form **covalent bonds** with other **carbon** atoms, resulting in long chains, branched chains, or closed rings. This ability is due to the very strong **carbon-carbon** bond energy. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct regarding catenation.***
 
• **Tetravalency** refers to the fact that **carbon** has **4** valence electrons in its outermost shell. This allows a single **carbon** atom to form four chemical bonds with other atoms like **hydrogen**, **oxygen**, **nitrogen**, or **sulfur**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct regarding tetravalency.***
 
• The **small size** of the **carbon** atom allows its nucleus to hold the shared pairs of electrons strongly. This results in the formation of exceptionally stable and strong bonds, which is a major factor in the existence of a vast number of **carbon compounds**.
 
• **Carbon** primarily forms **covalent bonds** rather than **ionic bonds**. This is because **carbon** has **4** electrons in its valence shell, and losing or gaining **4** electrons would require a massive amount of energy. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Carbon** is a **non-metal** and has a relatively **low atomic mass** of **12** and a **small atomic size**. These properties are opposite to what is suggested in some incorrect options. ***Hence, statements 3 and 4 are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Organic Chemistry**: This is the dedicated branch of chemistry that deals with the study of **carbon** and its compounds. Today, millions of **organic compounds** are known to scientists, far exceeding the number of compounds formed by all other elements combined.
 
• **Isomerism**: Due to its unique bonding capabilities, **carbon** compounds often exhibit **isomerism**, where molecules have the same chemical formula but different structural arrangements, further increasing the diversity of **carbon** structures.
 
• **Atomic Properties**: **Carbon** has the **atomic number 6** and its **electronic configuration** is **2, 4**. It belongs to **Group 14** and **Period 2** of the **Modern Periodic Table**.
 
• **Allotropes of Carbon**: **Carbon** exists in various forms in nature called **allotropes**. The most common ones include **Diamond** (the hardest natural substance), **Graphite** (a good conductor of electricity), and **Buckminsterfullerene** (a spherical molecule with **60** carbon atoms).
 
• **Functional Groups**: **Carbon** chains can be attached to various **functional groups** such as **alcohol (-OH)**, **aldehyde (-CHO)**, **carboxylic acid (-COOH)**, and **ketones (>C=O)**, which determine the chemical properties of the resulting **organic compounds**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **C-C bond energy** is approximately **348 kJ/mol**, which is significantly higher compared to other elements like **Silicon** (approx. **297 kJ/mol**), explaining why **carbon** shows the highest degree of **catenation**.
 
• **Hydrocarbons** are the simplest **carbon** compounds, consisting only of **carbon** and **hydrogen**. They are classified into **Saturated** (alkanes) and **Unsaturated** (alkenes and alkynes) based on the presence of single, double, or triple bonds.
 
• In **2024**, **carbon** remains the backbone of life and **biotechnology**, as it is found in **DNA**, **proteins**, **carbohydrates**, and **fats**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relation between frequency (v)and time period ( T )?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**v T = 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Frequency (v)** is defined as the **number of complete oscillations** or cycles of a wave that occur in a **unit of time** (usually **one second**).
 
• **Time Period (T)** is defined as the **time taken** by a wave to complete **one full cycle** or oscillation.
 
• The relationship between **frequency** and **time period** is **reciprocal**. This means that as the time period of a wave increases, its frequency decreases, and vice versa.
 
• Mathematically, this relationship is expressed as **v = 1/T**. When we rearrange this equation by multiplying both sides by **T**, we get the product **v T = 1**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• If the relationship was **v T = 0**, it would imply that either the frequency or the time duration is **zero**, which is not possible for a physical wave. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The expression **v / T = 1** suggests that frequency and time period are **directly proportional** and equal, which contradicts the laws of physics. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The expression **v + T = 1** is incorrect because **frequency (1/s)** and **time (s)** have different physical dimensions and cannot be added together in a standard physical equation. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SI Units**: The **SI unit** of **frequency** is the **Hertz (Hz)**, named after the **German physicist Heinrich Rudolf Hertz**. **1 Hz** is equal to **1 cycle per second**. The unit of the **Time Period** is the **second (s)**.
 
• **Wave Speed Formula**: The speed of a wave is determined by its **frequency** and **wavelength (λ)**, represented by the formula **Speed = v × λ**.
 
• **Angular Frequency**: In many physics applications, **angular frequency (ω)** is used, which is related to frequency by the formula **ω = 2πv** or **ω = 2π/T**. It is measured in **radians per second**.
 
• **Audible Range**: For a human ear, the standard **audible frequency range** is between **20 Hz** and **20,000 Hz**. A frequency of **20 Hz** corresponds to a **Time Period** of **0.05 seconds**.
 
• **Dimensional Analysis**: In **dimensional formulas**, **Time (T)** has the dimension **[T]**, and **Frequency (v)** has the dimension **[T⁻¹]**. Their product results in a **dimensionless constant** of **1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Inverse Relationship**: A high-frequency wave (like **Ultraviolet rays**) has a very **short time period**, whereas a low-frequency wave (like **Radio waves**) has a **long time period**.
 
• **Periodic Motion**: This relationship is fundamental to all types of **periodic motion**, including the movement of a **simple pendulum**, the vibration of a **guitar string**, and **electromagnetic radiation**.
 
• **Practical Application**: In **electronics**, the clock speed of a **processor** is measured in **Gigahertz (GHz)**. A **1 GHz** processor completes **1,000,000,000 cycles** in **one second**, meaning the **Time Period** for a single cycle is **1 nanosecond (10⁻⁹ s)**.

questions.question: Which of the following happens when the distances between roots and leaves become large in plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diffusion becomes insufficient.**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• In plants with small body designs, energy and raw materials can easily move to all parts of the plant body through the process of **diffusion**. 
• However, if the **distance between the roots and the leaves** becomes large—which occurs as the plant grows in size and complexity—the process of **diffusion becomes insufficient** to provide raw materials to the leaves and energy to the roots. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.*** 
• **Diffusion** is a passive, relatively slow process that works efficiently only over **short distances** (cellular level or across a few cells). It cannot meet the high metabolic demands of large multicellular organisms like tall trees. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*** 
• To overcome this limitation, plants have evolved a dedicated **transportation system** consisting of **vascular tissues** to move substances over long distances. 
• While the distance increases, the **roots continue to absorb water**; however, without a specialized system, that water would never reach the canopy. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*** 
• The production of **chlorophyll** is primarily dependent on **light availability, genetics, and mineral nutrients** (like Magnesium and Iron) rather than the physical distance between plant organs. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*** 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Vascular System in Plants:** 
• To manage **long-distance transport**, plants utilize two specialized tissues: **Xylem** and **Phloem**. 
• **Xylem** is responsible for the **unidirectional transport** of **water and minerals** from the **roots** to the **leaves**. It consists of **tracheids** and **vessels** which form a continuous system of water-conducting channels. 
• **Phloem** facilitates **translocation**, which is the movement of soluble products of **photosynthesis** (like **sucrose** and **amino acids**) from the **leaves** to storage organs and growing parts of the plant. This transport is **bidirectional**. 
• **Mechanism of Water Movement:** 
• At the **roots**, cells in contact with the soil actively take up **ions**, creating a concentration gradient that pulls water into the root (**Root Pressure**). 
• For very tall plants, **transpiration pull** acts as the main driving force. As water evaporates through the **stomata** in the leaves, it creates a suction that pulls water columns upward through the **xylem**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Energy Needs:** Large plants have a high proportion of **dead cells** (in tissues like xylem), which results in relatively **low energy needs** compared to animals, allowing them to survive with slower transport systems despite the large distances. 
• **Diffusion vs. Bulk Flow:** **Diffusion** relies on **random molecular motion**, whereas the transport in vascular plants is a **bulk flow** or **mass flow** system driven by pressure differences. 
• **Distance Impact:** If a plant relied solely on **diffusion** to transport water, it is estimated that it would take **years** for a single molecule of water to travel from the roots to the top of a tall tree.

questions.question: A chemical reaction in which two or more substances combine to form a single product is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**combination reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **combination reaction**, also known as a **synthesis reaction**, is a process where **two or more elements or compounds** react to form a **single new substance**. ***Hence, the correct answer is combination reaction.***
 
• The general chemical representation for this type of reaction is **A + B → AB**, where A and B are the **reactants** and AB is the **sole product**.
 
• These reactions are predominantly **exothermic** in nature because the formation of **new chemical bonds** typically releases **energy** in the form of **heat** or **light**.
 
• A classic example is the **burning of coal**, where solid **Carbon (C)** reacts with **Oxygen (O₂)** from the air to produce **Carbon Dioxide (CO₂)** gas.
 
• Another common instance is the reaction between **Quicklime (Calcium Oxide, CaO)** and **water (H₂O)** to form **Slaked Lime (Calcium Hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂)**, which is characterized by the evolution of a large amount of **heat**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Decomposition Reaction**: 
 
 
• This is the **opposite** of a combination reaction, where a **single reactant** breaks down into **two or more simpler products**.
 
• It usually requires **energy** in the form of **heat, light, or electricity** to break the existing bonds. For example, **Calcium Carbonate (CaCO₃)** decomposes into **Calcium Oxide (CaO)** and **Carbon Dioxide (CO₂)** when heated. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Displacement Reaction**: 
 
 
• In this reaction, a **more reactive element** displaces or removes a **less reactive element** from its compound or **salt solution**.
 
• A well-known example is **Iron (Fe)** reacting with **Copper Sulfate (CuSO₄)** solution, where Iron displaces Copper to form **Iron Sulfate (FeSO₄)** and solid **Copper**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Double Displacement Reaction**: 
 
 
• This involves an **exchange of ions** between **two compounds** to form two new substances.
 
• Often, one of the products is a **precipitate** (an insoluble solid). For example, **Sodium Sulfate (Na₂SO₄)** reacts with **Barium Chloride (BaCl₂)** to form **Barium Sulfate (BaSO₄)** precipitate and **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Industrial Applications**: Combination reactions are vital in the **Haber Process** for the industrial production of **Ammonia (NH₃)**, where **Nitrogen** and **Hydrogen** gases combine under high **pressure** and **temperature**.
 
• **Nature of Reactants**: Combination reactions can occur between **two elements** (like H₂ and O₂), **two compounds** (like CaO and H₂O), or an **element and a compound** (like CO and O₂).
 
• **Oxidation-Reduction (Redox)**: Many combination reactions are also **Redox reactions**, where there is a simultaneous **loss and gain of electrons** between the reacting species.
 
• **Law of Conservation of Mass**: In every chemical reaction, including combination reactions, the **total mass** of the reactants must equal the **total mass** of the products, necessitating the **balancing of chemical equations**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the properties of a liquid?

options.text: No fixed shape, no fixed volume

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**No fixed shape, fixed volume**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Matter** in the **liquid state** is characterized by its ability to **flow** and change **shape**, but it maintains a **constant volume** under consistent **temperature** and **pressure**.
 
• A liquid has **no fixed shape** because the **kinetic energy** of its particles is high enough to overcome the **rigid bonds** seen in solids. This allows particles to slide past one another, meaning the liquid takes the shape of whatever **container** it occupies.
 
• Liquids possess a **fixed volume** because the **intermolecular forces of attraction** are still strong enough to keep the particles close together. Unlike **gases**, the particles in a liquid do not have enough energy to completely escape the attraction of their neighbors.
 
• Because the particles are packed closely, liquids have **very low compressibility**. This means that even under high **pressure**, the **volume** of a liquid remains virtually **unchanged**.

questions.question: Which of the following rules determines the direction of the magnetic field produced by a current carrying circular loop?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right-Hand Thumb rule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Right-Hand Thumb rule**, also known as **Maxwell’s Corkscrew Rule**, is the fundamental principle used to determine the direction of the **magnetic field** associated with a **current-carrying conductor**, including a **circular loop**.
 
• According to this rule, if you imagine holding a current-carrying straight conductor in your **right hand** such that the **thumb points** in the direction of the **current**, then your **fingers** will wrap around the conductor in the direction of the **field lines** of the magnetic field.
 
• When applied to a **circular loop**, every section of the wire generates magnetic field lines in the form of **concentric circles**. By applying the **Right-Hand Thumb rule** to any segment of the loop, one can see that the field lines inside the loop all point in the **same direction**.
 
• At the **center of the circular loop**, these magnetic field lines appear as **straight lines**. The strength of the magnetic field produced is directly proportional to the **amount of current** flowing through the loop and the **number of turns** in the coil.
 
• The direction of the magnetic field depends on the direction of the current; if the current flows in a **clockwise direction**, the magnetic field enters the face of the loop (acting as a **South Pole**), and if it flows **anticlockwise**, the field emerges from it (acting as a **North Pole**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fleming's Left-Hand Rule:**
 
 
• This rule is primarily used to find the direction of the **magnetic force** acting on a moving charge or a current-carrying wire placed in an external magnetic field.
 
• It is the working principle behind **electric motors**.
 
• The **thumb** represents the direction of the **force (motion)**, the **forefinger** represents the **magnetic field**, and the **middle finger** represents the **current**.
 
 
 
• **Fleming's Right-Hand Rule:**
 
 
• This rule is used to determine the direction of the **induced current** when a conductor moves inside a magnetic field.
 
• It is the fundamental principle for **electric generators**.
 
• The **thumb** points in the direction of the **motion of the conductor**, the **forefinger** in the direction of the **magnetic field**, and the **middle finger** indicates the direction of the **induced current**.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field of a Solenoid:**
 
 
• A **solenoid** is a long coil containing a large number of close turns of insulated copper wire.
 
• The magnetic field produced by a solenoid is similar to that of a **bar magnet**, with one end behaving as a **magnetic North pole** and the other as a **magnetic South pole**.
 
• The **Right-Hand Thumb rule** is also used here to visualize the field lines looping through the center of the coil.
 
 
 
• **SI Units and Constants:**
 
 
• The **SI unit** of magnetic field strength (magnetic flux density) is the **Tesla (T)**.
 
• The magnetic effect of current was first discovered by **H.C. Oersted** in **1820**, proving the link between **electricity and magnetism**.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms will accumulate maximum concentration of DDT?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Human**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The phenomenon of the progressive increase in the concentration of a non-biodegradable toxicant at each successive trophic level is known as **Biological Magnification** or **Biomagnification**.
 
• **DDT (Dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane)** is a well-known **non-biodegradable** pesticide that is fat-soluble and cannot be metabolized or excreted by organisms effectively.
 
• In a typical food chain, the concentration of **DDT** increases as it moves from producers to top consumers.
 
 
• **Grass**: Being a **producer** (Trophic Level 1), it contains the lowest concentration of the chemical as it absorbs it from the soil or water. ***Hence, this option is incorrect for maximum concentration.***
 
• **Goat**: As a **primary consumer** (Trophic Level 2) that feeds on grass, the concentration of **DDT** increases in its body tissues compared to the grass. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
• **Spider**: Usually acting as a **secondary consumer** (Trophic Level 3) or predator, it would have a higher concentration than its prey, but still lower than top-tier predators. <span
